title: A local conormal wedge lies locally in the span of affine ideal-unit wedges
statement: Let i:Z→Y be a closed immersion [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], V an affine open of Y, N=i*ker(i) [def-pc-module-pullback, def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], E=∧^n N [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power], and η:ker(i)→i_*N the canonical tensor-pullback adjunction unit [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Let W⊆i⁻¹V be open, a:Fin(n)→Γ(W,N), and x∈W. There is W′⊆W containing x such that the restriction of the canonical exterior-sheaf section wedge(a) to W′ belongs to the Γ(Z,W′)-linear span of the sections wedge((η_V(b_j))|W′), with b:Fin(n)→Γ(V,ker(i)). This is a statement of span membership for one wedge, not a coordinate compatibility assertion.

source.place: Tag 01R3 (1),(2), Tag 0096 and affine module localization; parent proof step 3, the finite local lifting and denominator-clearing part.

proof.text: Use affine_conormal_sections to obtain quasi-coherence of N and the unit-normalized affine equivalence Γ(N,i⁻¹V)≅I/I². Surjectivity of I→I/I² and range_toModulesι_app lift every chart conormal section to an ideal section on V. Hence the component η_V is surjective.

Choose a basic open D(f) in the affine closed chart containing x and contained in W. Apply exists_map_eq_pow_smul_of_isAffineOpen to the restriction of each a_j to D(f). Obtain m_j and t_j on the full closed chart with t_j|D(f)=f^m_j a_j|D(f). Lift each t_j along the surjective unit to b_j. The restricted f is a unit, so a_j|D(f)=f^(-m_j)(η_V b_j)|D(f).

Naturality of the sheafification unit and exterior-power restriction identifies the restricted wedge with the wedge of the restricted entries. AlternatingMap.map_smul_univ expresses this as the product of the inverse denominator coefficients times the generator wedge indexed by b. Submodule.subset_span and smul_mem prove the span membership. This also covers n=0 because empty products are one.

lean.statement:
theorem conormal_wedge_mem_span_locally
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i] (n : ℕ)
    (V : Y.affineOpens) (W : Z.Opens) (hW : W ≤ i ⁻¹ᵁ V.1)
    (a : Fin n → ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules).val.obj (op W))
    (x : Z) (hx : x ∈ W) :
    let N := (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules
    let E := Scheme.Modules.exteriorPower N n
    let η := (Classical.choose (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction i)).unit.app
      i.ker.toModules
    ∃ (W' : Z.Opens) (hW' : W' ≤ W), x ∈ W' ∧
      E.val.map (homOfLE hW').op (wedge (M := N) (r := n) (U := W) a) ∈
        Submodule.span (Z.presheaf.obj (op W'))
          (Set.range (fun b : Fin n → i.ker.toModules.val.obj (op V.1) ↦
            wedge (M := N) (r := n) (U := W')
              (fun j ↦ N.val.map (homOfLE (hW'.trans hW)).op
                (η.val.app (op V.1) (b j)))))
lean.note: Retired the local duplicate in favour of the upstream theorem. The exterior presheaves agree by exteriorSheafPresheaf_eq_exteriorPower. Pairing each presheaf with its pure-wedge maps identifies the whole sheafified span predicate, so the sole direct consumer preserves its original exteriorSheaf statement.
